newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to sell 50 bln dong T-bills on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to sell 50 bln dong T-bills on Wednesday.

text.p: Vietnam will auction 50 billion dong ($4.51 million) worth of six-month Treasury bills on Wednesday, an official at the State Bank of Vietnam said on Monday.
At the last sale of government paper, on November 20, the central bank issued 2.9 billion dong worth of one-year notes to domestic institutions at an annual rate of 8.00 percent.
There have been 16 such sales so far this year, through which a total of 903.9 billion dong worth of Treasury stock has been issued.

Rates fell sharply in the first half of this year, partly due to a dong surplus in the banking system. At the first sale of the year, on March 1, the state bank sold six-month bills at a rate of 15.00 percent.

However, rates have bottomed out in the past few weeks due to tighter liquidity conditions and bids for stock have come in far higher than the Ministry of Finance was prepared to accept. As a result, much less stock has been allocated at recent auctions than the central bank had originally offered.
